business_problem: Bollore Transport & Logistics needed to break down siloed global systems and growing local microservices into a consistent architecture that could handle special freight cases and country-specific regulatory requirements.
solution_summary: Bollore Transport & Logistics created an enterprise-microservices architecture on MongoDB to standardize how services and data are exposed across its global logistics business. Each microservice combines an API exposure layer, a cloud-native execution engine, and a MongoDB-managed single source of truth for the business entity it owns, such as quotation or order-form workflows. This pattern lets the company virtualize and normalize data from historically separate subsidiaries and departments without eliminating manual services or rewriting every legacy package. MongoDB Atlas underpins the architecture with horizontal scalability, sharding, and TTL support, while the same enterprise microservices are being positioned as data sources for a future lakehouse and a lakehouse-as-a-service model. The result is a reusable blueprint that removes single points of failure and gives Bollore a flexible way to add track-and-trace, courier, customer-preference, and carbon-data services over time.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Acts as the single source of truth for Bollore's enterprise microservices and provides the scaling features behind the new pattern.

data_flow: Requests enter through portal or manual service channels, are virtualized and standardized by enterprise microservices, stored in MongoDB-backed repositories for business entities such as quotations and orders, and then passed to service producers and, over time, to lakehouse-style analytical services.
business_outcome: Bollore gained a resilient architecture pattern that can unify logistics services, support country-specific requirements, and expand digital freight capabilities without multiplying operational fragility.
